levels.question: Tap the biggest number.
levels.screen: Three numbers: a giant 9, a medium 6 and a tiny 15.
levels.solution: Tap the tiny 15.
levels.why: 15 is the biggest number even though it is drawn the smallest.

levels.question: Turn on the light.
levels.screen: A dark room, a light switch on the wall, and a lamp with its plug lying on the floor next to the socket.
levels.solution: Drag the plug into the socket, then tap the switch.
hints: The switch works fine. Something else is missing.
Check the floor near the wall.
levels.why: A lamp needs power before the switch can do anything.

levels.question: Help the cat get some sleep.
levels.screen: A cat on a bed, squinting. Bright sunlight comes through an open window with curtains pulled to the side.
levels.solution: Drag the curtains closed.
hints: The sun is too bright. Block it.
levels.why: Closing the curtains makes the room dark enough to sleep.

levels.question: How many eggs are there?
levels.screen: An egg carton with the lid half closed. Six eggs are visible.
levels.solution: Drag the lid fully open and count 12 eggs. Type 12.
hints: Are you seeing the whole carton?
levels.why: The lid was hiding the second row of eggs.

levels.question: Wake up Dad.
levels.screen: Dad snoring in bed. An alarm clock on the nightstand. Tapping the clock does nothing.
levels.solution: Shake the phone. The alarm clock rattles and rings, and Dad wakes up.
levels.fallback: Web: tap the alarm clock 5 times quickly.
hints: The clock needs a bigger push than a tap.
levels.why: Shaking the phone shakes the clock.

levels.question: Find the TV remote.
levels.screen: A living room with a sofa, a coffee table, a plant and a TV.
levels.solution: Drag the sofa cushion aside. The remote is under it.
hints: Where does everyone lose the remote?
levels.why: The remote is always in the sofa.

levels.question: Make a cup of tea.
levels.screen: A kettle, an empty cup and a tea bag on the kitchen counter.
levels.solution: Drag the tea bag into the cup, tap the kettle to boil it, then drag the kettle over the cup to pour.
levels.why: Tea needs a tea bag and boiling water, in that order.

levels.question: Tap the odd one out.
levels.screen: Four clocks showing 3:00, 6:00, 9:00 and 12:30.
levels.solution: Tap the clock showing 12:30.
hints: Three clocks show an exact hour.
levels.why: Every clock is on the hour except 12:30.

levels.question: The baby is crying. Make it stop.
levels.screen: A crying baby in a crib. No toys or bottles anywhere.
levels.solution: Drag the letter 'o' from the word 'stop' in the question into the baby's mouth as a pacifier.
hints: There's nothing in the room you can use.
The question itself can be touched.
levels.why: The round 'o' looks just like a pacifier.

levels.question: Water the plant.
levels.screen: A droopy plant. An empty watering can and a sink with a broken tap. A rain cloud is visible through the window.
levels.solution: Drag the rain cloud from outside the window over the plant. It rains on the plant.
hints: The tap and the can are useless.
levels.why: The cloud is a movable object, and clouds carry water.

levels.question: How many legs can you see?
levels.screen: A dog sitting on a chair.
levels.solution: Type 8.
levels.why: The dog has 4 legs and the chair has 4 legs.

levels.question: Dry the wet sock.
levels.screen: A dripping sock and a washing machine with a dial set to WASH.
levels.solution: Drag the sock into the machine and turn the dial to DRY.
hints: The machine can do more than wash.
levels.why: Many washing machines can also dry clothes.

levels.question: Catch the mouse.
levels.screen: A mouse running around the kitchen, too fast to tap. A mousetrap in the corner and a piece of cheese on the table.
levels.solution: Drag the cheese onto the trap. The mouse runs into it.
hints: You can't catch it by hand.
Give the mouse a reason to go into the trap.
levels.why: Bait makes the mouse come to you.

levels.question: Who ate the cake?
levels.screen: A boy, a dog and Grandma sitting around an empty cake plate. Everyone looks innocent.
levels.solution: Pinch to zoom in on Grandma's lap. It's covered in cake crumbs. Tap Grandma.
levels.why: The crumbs give her away.

levels.question: Get the cookie jar from the top shelf.
levels.screen: A cookie jar on a very high shelf. A short kid and a chair that is too low.
levels.solution: Turn the phone upside down. The jar slides off the shelf and the kid catches it.
levels.fallback: Web: tap the two screws on the shelf to loosen them and the jar slides down.
hints: The kid will never reach it.
What if the room were upside down?
levels.why: Turning the phone turns the room, so the jar falls.

levels.question: Turn off all the lights.
levels.screen: A room with 4 glowing lamps and a phone lying on the table with its screen lit.
levels.solution: Tap all 4 lamps, then tap the glowing phone on the table.
hints: The room still isn't dark after the lamps are off.
levels.why: A phone screen is also a light.

levels.question: Which is heavier: 1 kg of feathers or 1 kg of iron?
levels.screen: Buttons: Feathers / Iron / Same.
levels.solution: Tap 'Same'.
levels.why: Both weigh exactly 1 kg.

levels.question: Feed the fish.
levels.screen: A hungry fish in a tank and a box of fish food above it. Tapping the box does nothing.
levels.solution: Drag the box over the tank and swipe it left and right quickly to sprinkle the food.
hints: How do you get food out of a shaker?
Shake it from side to side.
levels.why: Fish food comes out when you shake the box.

levels.question: Put all 5 toys away.
levels.screen: A toy box. A ball, a car, blocks and a doll are on the floor. A teddy bear's ear pokes out from behind the curtain.
levels.solution: Drag the 4 visible toys into the box, then drag the curtain aside and put the teddy bear in.
hints: Something is hiding behind the curtain.
levels.why: The fifth toy was hidden.

levels.question: The dog is barking too loudly. Make it quiet.
levels.screen: A barking dog with sound waves. Petting it and giving it a bone don't work.
levels.solution: Press the phone's volume-down button until it's muted.
levels.fallback: Web: tap the speaker icon in the game's top bar.
hints: Control the sound, not the dog.
levels.why: Muting your phone silences the dog.

levels.question: How many holes does this T-shirt have?
levels.screen: A plain T-shirt lying flat.
levels.solution: Type 4.
hints: Think about where your body goes in.
levels.why: One for the neck, two for the arms, one at the bottom.

levels.question: Fix the clock.
levels.screen: A wall clock showing the wrong time, with '+1 hour' and '+5 min' buttons.
levels.solution: Use the buttons to set the clock to the real time on your phone (within 5 minutes).
hints: What time is it right now?
Check the time on your phone.
levels.why: A fixed clock shows the real time.

levels.question: Help Mom find her glasses.
levels.screen: Mom searching a messy room. The glasses are pushed up on top of her head.
levels.solution: Tap the top of Mom's head.
levels.why: The glasses were on her head all along.

levels.question: Bake the cake. The guests arrive in 5 seconds!
levels.screen: A bowl of batter, an oven with a dial, and a kitchen timer showing 60:00.
levels.solution: Drag the batter into the oven, turn the dial on, then spin the timer down to 0:00.
hints: You don't have time to wait an hour.
levels.why: Spinning the timer skips the wait.

levels.question: Get out of the house! The door is locked.
levels.screen: A locked front door, a rug, a wall clock and a drawer.
levels.solution: 1) Tap the clock. A drawer pops open with a note saying 'Under your feet'. 2) Drag the rug aside to find a giant key. 3) Pinch or double-tap the key to shrink it. 4) Drag the key to the door.
hints: The note talks about the floor. The key is too big: pinch it (or double-tap it) to make it smaller.
levels.why: World finale: it combines tapping, dragging and pinching.

levels.question: Make this true: 1 + 1 = 3
levels.screen: The equation 1 + 1 = 3 on a blackboard.
levels.solution: Tap the '=' sign. It changes to '≠'.
levels.why: 1 + 1 ≠ 3 is a true statement.

levels.question: What is half of 8? Find 3 answers.
levels.screen: A big number 8 and three empty answer boxes.
levels.solution: Type 4, 0 and 3.
hints: One answer is maths. The others are about shape.
Cut the 8 across the middle, then down the middle.
levels.why: 8 ÷ 2 = 4. The top half of an 8 looks like 0, and the right half looks like 3.

levels.question: How many triangles?
levels.screen: A big triangle divided into 4 small triangles (3 in the corners and 1 upside down in the middle).
levels.solution: Type 5.
levels.why: 4 small triangles plus the big one.

levels.question: What has keys but can't open locks?
levels.screen: A classroom with a piano in the corner.
levels.solution: Type 'piano' (also accept 'keyboard').
levels.why: A piano has keys, but not the kind for doors.

levels.screen: Teacher at the blackboard. Typing 18 makes the teacher shake their head. A round wall clock hangs above the board.
levels.solution: Type 6.
hints: The teacher wants a different kind of maths. Look around the room.
Count 9 hours forward from 9 o'clock on the clock.
levels.why: On a clock, 9 hours after 9 o'clock is 6 o'clock.

levels.question: Cut the cake into 4 equal pieces.
levels.screen: A round cake viewed from above and a knife icon.
levels.solution: Swipe one line straight across, then a second line across it to make a cross.
levels.why: Two cuts through the middle make 4 equal pieces.

levels.question: Tap the student who isn't paying attention.
levels.screen: Five students reading. One is holding their book upside down.
levels.solution: Tap the student with the upside-down book.
hints: Check how the books are held.
levels.why: Nobody can really read a book upside down.

levels.question: Move ONE matchstick to fix the equation: 6 + 4 = 4
levels.screen: The equation made of matchsticks.
levels.solution: Move the middle matchstick of the 6 into the empty gap to make a 0. Now it reads 0 + 4 = 4.
hints: A 6 is one matchstick away from a 0.

levels.question: What comes next? 1, 2, 4, 8, ...
levels.screen: The number sequence on the board.
levels.solution: Type 16.
hints: How does each number get bigger?

levels.question: What comes next? 1, 11, 21, 1211, ...
levels.screen: The sequence on the board.
hints: Don't do maths. Read each number out loud.
levels.why: 1211 is one 1, one 2, two 1s → 111221.

levels.question: Help Sam copy the homework from the board.
levels.screen: A student at the back of a big classroom. The writing on the board is a tiny blur.
levels.solution: Pinch to zoom in on the board.
hints: The board is too far away.
Make it bigger with two fingers.
levels.why: Zooming in makes the board readable.

levels.question: Which pencil is the longest?
levels.screen: Three pencils with arrow-shaped ends that make them look different lengths.
levels.solution: Drag the pencils next to each other. They're the same length. Tap 'Same'.
levels.why: An optical illusion. The arrow ends trick your brain.

levels.question: Make 100 using four 9s.
levels.screen: Four '9' tiles and +, −, ×, ÷ tiles.

levels.question: Ring the school bell.
levels.screen: A bell high on the wall with a rope too high to reach. A closed cleaning cupboard.
levels.solution: Tap the cupboard to open it, drag the ladder under the bell, then tap the rope.
levels.why: The ladder was stored in the cupboard.

levels.question: Pass the exam!
levels.screen: An exam paper with a tiny line of text and an answer box. A name plate on the desk says 'LEO'.
levels.solution: Zoom in on the paper. The question says 'What is your name?' Type LEO.
hints: You have to read the question first.
Zoom in, then look at the desk.
levels.why: The easiest exam ever, once you can read it.

levels.question: How many months have 28 days?
levels.screen: A calendar on the wall.
levels.solution: Type 12.
levels.why: Every month has at least 28 days.

levels.question: Tap the shape with the most sides.
levels.screen: A triangle, a square, a hexagon and a 5-point star.
levels.solution: Tap the star.
hints: The hexagon is not the answer.
Count the edges around the star.
levels.why: A 5-point star has 10 sides.

levels.question: Get exactly 4 litres of water.
levels.screen: A 3-litre jug and a 5-litre jug, each with Fill and Empty buttons. Drag one jug onto the other to pour.
levels.solution: Fill the 5. Pour into the 3 (leaves 2). Empty the 3. Pour the 2 into the 3. Fill the 5. Pour into the 3 until full (1 goes in). 4 litres are left in the 5.
hints: Try to get 2 litres into the small jug first.
levels.why: A classic jug puzzle, solved by pouring back and forth.

levels.question: Wake up the sleeping student.
levels.screen: A student asleep on their desk with a feather on the desk next to their nose.
levels.solution: Blow into the microphone. The feather tickles their nose and they sneeze awake.
levels.fallback: Web: drag the feather back and forth under their nose.
levels.why: The microphone hears you blowing.

levels.question: What is the answer?
levels.screen: An empty blackboard and an answer box. Nothing else.
levels.solution: Type 45, which is the level number shown at the top of the screen.
hints: The answer is already on your screen.
Look at the top of the screen.
levels.why: The only number on screen is the level number.

levels.question: Add ONE line to make it true: 5 + 5 + 5 = 550
levels.screen: The equation on the board and a chalk tool.
levels.solution: Draw a small line on the first '+' to turn it into a 4: 545 + 5 = 550.
hints: The line doesn't have to be straight across.

levels.question: Which word is always spelled WRONG?
levels.screen: An open dictionary with several words. An answer box.
levels.solution: Type 'wrong' (or tap the word WRONG in the question).
hints: The answer is in the question.
levels.why: The word 'wrong' is always spelled W-R-O-N-G.

levels.question: How many sides does a circle have?
levels.screen: Buttons: 0 / 1 / 2 / Infinite.
levels.solution: Tap 2.
hints: Think about where you can be compared to a circle.
levels.why: An inside and an outside.

levels.question: Sort the books from shortest to tallest.
levels.screen: Four books standing up and one lying flat on its side.
levels.solution: Tap the flat book to stand it up. It's the tallest, so put it last.
hints: One book isn't standing like the others.
Stand up the lying book first.
levels.why: You can't compare a book's height while it's lying down.

levels.question: Escape from detention!
levels.screen: A classroom door with a 3-digit keypad, three coloured sticky notes (red, blue, green), a board, a clock and a window.
levels.solution: Red note: 'Board'. The board says ? × 2 = 14, so 7. Blue note: 'Clock'. The hour hand points to 3. Green note: 'Window'. There are 5 birds outside. Enter 7-3-5.
hints: Each sticky note points to one digit.
Order: red, blue, green. Solve the board, read the clock, count the birds.
levels.why: World finale: maths, reading and observation together.

levels.question: The thief ran through the muddy garden. Who is it?
levels.screen: Three suspects. Only one has muddy shoes.
levels.solution: Tap the suspect with muddy shoes.
levels.why: The mud is the evidence.

levels.question: Find the fingerprint.
levels.screen: A desk with a lamp, a book, a glass of water and a magnifying glass.
levels.solution: Drag the magnifying glass over the glass of water to reveal a fingerprint. Tap it.
hints: Prints show up best on glass.
levels.why: Fingerprints stick to smooth surfaces like glass.

levels.question: One suspect is lying. Who?
levels.screen: A: 'I was at the beach all day' (sunburned). B: 'I was baking' (flour on hands). C: 'I was reading in my room' (the room's light bulb is broken, and it was night).
levels.solution: Tap C.
hints: Check each story against the picture.
Can you read in the dark?
levels.why: C couldn't read at night with a broken bulb.

levels.question: Open the safe.
levels.screen: A safe with a 4-digit keypad. A calendar on the wall has April 12 circled with a heart.
levels.solution: Type 0412.
hints: People often use special dates as codes.
levels.why: The owner used an anniversary as the code: month 04, day 12.

levels.question: The witness drew the thief. Who is it?
levels.screen: A strange drawing and four suspects. The drawing doesn't look like anyone.
levels.solution: Tap the drawing to turn it the right way up. It's a face with a beard, which matches suspect 3. Tap them.
hints: The drawing is correct. Maybe it's being held wrong.
levels.why: The witness handed it over upside down.

levels.question: Find the spare key.
levels.screen: A front door, a doormat, a flower pot and a lamp post.
levels.solution: Tap the flower pot to tip it over. The key is underneath.
hints: It's not under the doormat. Too obvious!
levels.why: Flower pots are a common hiding place for spare keys.

levels.question: Decode the message: 3-1-20
levels.screen: A note with the numbers and a hint card: A = 1.
levels.solution: Type CAT.

levels.question: Read the secret message.
levels.screen: A blank sheet of paper, a desk lamp and a painting on the wall.
levels.solution: Drag the paper under the lamp. Heat reveals 'BEHIND THE PAINTING'. Tap the painting.
levels.why: Some invisible inks appear when heated.

levels.question: Which footprint was made by this boot?
levels.screen: The bottom of a boot with a zigzag pattern on the left side. Three footprints, including one copy and one mirrored copy.
levels.solution: Tap the mirrored footprint.
hints: A footprint is like a stamp.
levels.why: The print on the ground is a mirror image of the sole.

levels.question: Catch the thief in the dark.
levels.screen: A completely black screen.
levels.solution: Drag your finger around the screen to shine a torch. The thief's shoes are under the curtain. Tap them.
hints: Your finger can be a torch.
levels.why: Exploring the darkness reveals the hiding place.

levels.question: What time did the robbery happen?
levels.screen: A broken wristwatch on the floor showing 9:40 with a cracked face.
levels.solution: Type 9:40.
levels.why: The watch stopped when it broke.

levels.question: How many police officers are in the room?
levels.screen: Four officers in uniform and a man in a coat with a badge on his belt.
levels.solution: Type 5.
hints: Not every officer wears a uniform.
levels.why: The man in the coat is a plain-clothes detective.

levels.question: The thief just left. Which cup did they drink from?
levels.screen: Three coffee cups. One is still steaming.
levels.solution: Tap the steaming cup.
levels.why: The hot cup was used most recently.

levels.question: Check the door handle for prints.
levels.screen: A door handle and a powder brush.
levels.solution: Swipe the brush back and forth over the handle until the prints appear.
levels.why: Detectives dust for prints with powder.

levels.question: Unlock the suspect's phone.
levels.screen: A phone with a 3×3 dot lock screen. Faint smudge marks on the screen.
levels.solution: Tilt or zoom to see the smudges, which make an 'L' shape. Draw an L: top-left, down to bottom-left, across to bottom-right.
levels.why: Greasy finger trails reveal the pattern.

levels.question: Find the stolen bone.
levels.screen: A dog sniffing. Paw prints lead off the right edge of the screen.
levels.solution: Swipe the scene left to follow the paw prints. Tap the bone behind a tree.
hints: The scene is bigger than your screen.
levels.why: The world keeps going beyond the screen.

levels.question: The more you take, the more you leave behind. What are they?
levels.screen: A sandy path.
levels.solution: Type 'footsteps' (also accept 'steps' or 'footprints').
levels.why: Every step you take leaves a footprint behind.

levels.question: When will the thieves meet?
levels.screen: A note with backwards writing and a small hand mirror.
levels.solution: Drag the mirror next to the note. It reads 'MEET AT 9'. Type 9.
levels.why: A mirror flips the writing back to normal.

levels.question: Who stole the diamond? It's the middle of summer.
levels.screen: Three suspects in T-shirts. One is wearing thick winter gloves.
levels.solution: Tap the suspect with gloves.
levels.why: Gloves in summer means hiding fingerprints.

levels.question: Find the secret room.
levels.screen: A bookshelf. Books have letters on their spines: P, E, X, O, N, R, A. A note says 'Say the magic word'.
levels.solution: Tap the books O, P, E, N in that order. The shelf swings open.
levels.why: The 'magic word' to open a door is OPEN.

levels.question: Triangle = 3, Square = 4, Pentagon = ?
levels.screen: The three shapes with the values.
levels.solution: Type 5.
levels.why: Each value is the number of sides.

levels.question: The thief escaped by car 10 minutes ago. Which car was it?
levels.screen: Three parked cars on a snowy night. One has no snow on its bonnet.
levels.solution: Tap the car without snow on its bonnet.
hints: What happens to a car's engine when it's driven?
levels.why: Its hot engine melted the snow.

levels.question: Take a clear photo of the suspect in the dark alley.
levels.screen: A camera viewfinder showing a dark alley. A flash icon (off) and a shutter button.
levels.solution: Tap the flash icon to turn it on, then tap the shutter.
levels.why: A flash lights up the scene.

levels.question: Which word doesn't belong? LISTEN, SILENT, ENLIST, TINSEL, SALINE
levels.screen: Five word cards.
levels.solution: Tap SALINE.
hints: Look at the letters, not the meanings.
Four words use exactly the same letters.
levels.why: LISTEN, SILENT, ENLIST and TINSEL are anagrams. SALINE has an 'A'.

levels.question: Solve the case!
levels.screen: A crime scene with three hidden clues and three suspect cards.
levels.solution: 1) Zoom on the floor: a size 42 shoe print. 2) Tap the window latch: a red thread. 3) Open the bin: a train ticket for 7:15. 4) Compare the suspect cards: only one wears size 42, owns a red scarf and has no alibi after 7:00. Drag them to 'ARREST'.
hints: Check the floor, the window and the bin.
levels.why: World finale: collect evidence, then deduce.

levels.question: Launch the rocket.
levels.screen: A big red LAUNCH button under a clear plastic cover.
levels.solution: Swipe the cover up, then tap the button.
levels.why: Real launch buttons have covers to stop accidents.

levels.question: Help the astronaut drink water.
levels.screen: An astronaut and a floating bubble of water.
levels.solution: Drag the water bubble to the astronaut's mouth.
levels.why: In zero gravity, water floats in blobs.

levels.question: Which planet is missing?
levels.screen: Planets in a row: Mercury, Venus, a big Moon, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.
levels.solution: Drag the Moon aside. Earth is hiding behind it. Tap Earth.
hints: Not everything in the row is a planet.
levels.why: The Moon was in front of Earth.

levels.question: Make the astronaut float.
levels.screen: An astronaut stuck to the floor wearing big magnetic boots.
levels.solution: Tap the boots to take them off.
levels.why: Magnetic boots hold astronauts to the floor.

levels.question: Call Earth.
levels.screen: A radio showing 'NO SIGNAL' and a signal bar.
levels.solution: Hold the phone up high and tilt it upward until the signal bar is full.
levels.fallback: Web: drag the radio's antenna up to its full length.
hints: Where do people go to get better signal?
Raise your phone towards the sky.
levels.why: Pointing the phone up points the antenna at Earth.

levels.question: How many stars can you see?
levels.screen: Five twinkling star shapes and a big bright Sun in the corner.
levels.solution: Type 6.
hints: Something big and bright is easy to forget.
What kind of object is the Sun?
levels.why: The Sun is a star too.

levels.question: The alien is sad. Cheer it up.
levels.screen: A green alien with a big frown.
levels.solution: Rotate the frown 180° to turn it into a smile.
levels.why: An upside-down frown is a smile.

levels.question: Dock the spaceship with the space station.
levels.screen: A ship turned sideways and a docking port.
levels.solution: Rotate the ship (two-finger twist or the rotate handle) to line it up, then drag it slowly into the port.
hints: It must face the right way.
levels.why: Docking needs the right angle and a gentle push.

levels.question: Which way is up in space?
levels.screen: Buttons: Up / Down / Left / There is no up.
levels.solution: Tap 'There is no up'.
levels.why: Without gravity pulling you, there's no up or down.

levels.question: Grow a plant on Mars.
levels.screen: A seed in red soil, a block of ice, a heater and a grow lamp (off).
levels.solution: Drag the ice onto the heater to melt it into water, pour the water on the seed, then tap the grow lamp.
levels.why: Mars has frozen water. Melt it and add light.

levels.question: Wake up the robot.
levels.screen: A sleeping robot facing you. Tapping it does nothing.
levels.solution: Swipe to spin the robot around. Flip the ON switch on its back.
hints: You only see one side of it.
levels.why: The power switch is on the back.

levels.question: Fix the broken satellite.
levels.screen: A satellite with a missing solar panel piece floating nearby.
levels.solution: Drag the floating panel into the gap.
levels.why: The panel completes the satellite.

levels.question: The alien says 'olleh'. What does it mean?
levels.screen: An alien with a speech bubble.
levels.solution: Type 'hello'.
levels.why: 'olleh' backwards is 'hello'.

levels.question: One of the astronauts is an alien. Find it.
levels.screen: A crowd of astronauts in helmets. One has two antennae poking out of its helmet.
levels.solution: Tap the astronaut with the antennae.
levels.why: Antennae give the alien away.

levels.question: Escape the black hole!
levels.screen: A rocket being pulled towards a swirling black hole. Tapping the engine doesn't help.
levels.solution: Drag the black hole itself off the edge of the screen.
hints: What if you move the danger instead?
levels.why: In this game, even a black hole can be moved.

levels.question: The astronaut weighs 60 kg on Earth. What does the scale show on the Moon?
levels.screen: An astronaut on a scale on the Moon. A note: 'Moon gravity = 1/6 of Earth'.
levels.solution: Type 10.
levels.why: The Moon's gravity is about one sixth of Earth's.

levels.question: Power up the space station.
levels.screen: A 4×4 grid of wire tiles between a battery and a light.
levels.solution: Tap tiles to rotate them until a single wire path connects the battery to the light.
hints: Every tile on the path must connect on both sides.
levels.why: A complete circuit makes the electricity flow.

levels.question: Say hello to the aliens.
levels.screen: An astronaut facing a group of aliens.
levels.solution: Swipe the astronaut's hand left and right to wave.
hints: How do you greet someone without words?
levels.why: Waving works everywhere, even in space.

levels.question: Help the crew sleep.
levels.screen: A space station cabin, very bright. The crew can't sleep.
levels.solution: Turn on dark mode on your phone. The cabin becomes dark.
levels.fallback: Web: drag the brightness slider on the cabin wall all the way down.
hints: There's no light switch in the room.
levels.why: The game follows your phone's light and dark setting.

levels.question: Refuel the rocket.
levels.screen: A fuel pump and a rocket. The hose is too short to reach.
levels.solution: Spread two fingers on the hose to stretch it, then drag the nozzle to the rocket.
levels.fallback: Web: drag the end of the hose to stretch it.
hints: Make it longer with two fingers.
levels.why: In this game the hose is stretchy.

levels.question: What colour is the daytime sky on Mars?
levels.screen: Buttons: Blue / Orange-brown / Green / Black.
levels.solution: Tap Orange-brown.
levels.why: Red dust makes the Mars sky orange-brown. Funnily enough, Mars sunsets look blue!

levels.question: The Mars rover has stopped. Get it moving.
levels.screen: A rover with dusty solar panels and a battery icon at 0%.
levels.solution: Swipe across the solar panels to wipe off the dust. The battery charges and the rover drives.
hints: The panels can't see the Sun.
levels.why: Dust blocks sunlight from the solar panels.

levels.question: Feed the hungry alien.
levels.screen: An alien refusing a burger, an apple and a pizza. A glowing lamp in the corner.
levels.solution: Drag the lamp to the alien. It eats light.
levels.why: This alien runs on light, like a plant.

levels.question: Prepare for landing. Set switches A, B and C.
levels.screen: Three switches and rules: 1) Exactly one switch is ON. 2) A is OFF. 3) C is ON only if A is ON.
levels.solution: A OFF, B ON, C OFF.
hints: Rule 2 tells you about A right away.
If A is OFF, rule 3 says C must be OFF.
levels.why: A is OFF, so C is OFF. Only one switch can be ON, so it's B.

levels.question: Return to Earth!
levels.screen: A spaceship cockpit with a dusty window, a navigation screen and a parachute handle.
levels.solution: 1) Swipe the window clean to see Earth. 2) The navigation screen asks 'How many holes in a T-shirt?' (from level 21). Type 4. 3) Pull the parachute handle down. The ship lands in the garden of the house from World 1.
levels.why: Grand finale: it brings the story back home and rewards players who remember.
